I was actually never very good at any actual Grand Theft Auto game. I tried San Andreas longer than the others but it did not hold my interest with the story missions. I did enjoy getting on the quad bike and tearing around, and the radio stations were funny the first time around. GTA 4 did not interest me except for a few of the songs.

Just Cause 3 was a great maneuver game -- whether those maneuvers were done in vehicles or in the wingsuit. Given the jetpack (which I believe was DLC) the game world was a joy. The shooting was good, but it peaked with the mulitple-simultanous-shot rocket launcher. My one major complaint is that everything in the main game happened outside. (The DLC had some meaningful interior missions.)

Saints Row the Third is something I just tried recently. It is better than Just Cause 3 insofar as the world feels like buildings have meaningful interiors. However, I am noting a lot of crashes, which tend to break up the otherwise wonderful pacing. I doubt that my driving skills have improved much, but the driving in Saints Row the Third seems much more enjoyable than the driving in most Grand Theft Auto clones. The music really resonates with me; it makes the world feel extremely immersive and convincing.

The Witcher 3 is a lot more serious-story-driven than any of the other games mentioned above, but I suppose it warrants a mention as a must-play open-world game. Fallout 4 has a rather open world, but it lacks good vehicles. The Fallout 4 jetpack is weak sauce without mods. However, Fallout 4's base building is more detailed than just capturing territories and hideouts in most Grand Theft Auto clones, and the music was good for the first 20 hours; I would have enjoyed much more diverse but appropriate music. Elex reminded me of Fallout 4 but did not hold my interest.

I actually don't spend enough time playing games to rattle off many of the open-world games that probably belong here. I only played Far Cry 2, for example, and the later games in that series probably merit my attention. I have not played the Mad Max sandbox game, but many critics claim that it does not add much new fun to the well-established open world genre.

Thoughts, game recommendations, and experiences are welcome.
The best Grand Theft Auto clones and their weaknesses

Does the Just Cause series really count? I mean… I guess. There’s a “law enforcement” mechanic. That’s about it, though. 4 is better than 3, which I really didn’t think would be the case given how quickly it was released (and immediately forgotten). The weather mechanics are impressive, the physics not chugging on my 12 year old computer was impressive, and I liked the improvements to the controls over 3. 2 was extremely fun, but also horribly repetitious. Shame the multiplayer is dead.

It's really all about car mods and driving in different environments and using different tactics to blow up other car patrols/bases. No "law enforcement" from a police standpoint, but there are enemy patrols and such that are constantly trying to end your retribution. Definitely play it if you can find it on sale.

Sleeping Dogs. It's basically a GTA clone if it were heavily inspired by kung-fu flicks. It takes place in Honk Kong, and has a great story. Mostly focused on hand-to-hand combat with heavy gunplay in certain missions, but most combat is melee with a fluid combat system similar to the Arkham series of games. It's an underrated gem, I couldn't recommend it enough.
